root_cause.text: In ntfs3’s `run_unpack()` (`fs/ntfs3/run.c`), the volume-range validation used unchecked `lcn + len` arithmetic, so a 64-bit integer overflow could wrap the end LCN and let out-of-volume run mappings bypass the `sbi->used.bitmap.nbits` boundary check.
root_cause.evidence: The patch replaces `if (lcn != SPARSE_LCN64 && lcn + len > sbi->used.bitmap.nbits)` with `check_add_overflow(lcn, len, &lcn_end)` followed by `lcn_end > sbi->used.bitmap.nbits`, and the commit message explicitly says the raw addition “can wrap around for large lcn and len values, bypassing the validation.”

agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch replaces `if (lcn != SPARSE_LCN64 && lcn + len > sbi->used.bitmap.nbits)` with `check_add_overflow(lcn, len, &lcn_end)` followed by `lcn_end > sbi->used.bitmap.nbits`, and the commit message explicitly says the raw addition “can wrap around for large lcn and len values, bypassing the validation.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix LCN range validation by adding overflow-safe bounds checking before rejecting out-of-volume mappings.
intent_record.what: The code changed the LCN range validation in `run_unpack()`. Instead of directly checking `lcn + len > sbi->used.bitmap.nbits` when `lcn != SPARSE_LCN64`, it now first computes `lcn_end` with `check_add_overflow(lcn, len, &lcn_end)`, returns `-EINVAL` on overflow, and then compares `lcn_end` against `sbi->used.bitmap.nbits` before rejecting out-of-volume ranges.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this prevents unsigned addition overflow from bypassing the bounds check or producing an incorrect wrapped-around end value. Valid ranges are still accepted, but malformed or too-large `lcn`/`len` combinations are now reliably rejected with `-EINVAL`.

grouping_result.intent: Fix LCN range validation by adding overflow-safe bounds checking before rejecting out-of-volume mappings.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it fixes unsafe LCN range validation in ntfs3 by adding overflow-safe bounds checking for lcn + len before accepting run mappings.

candidates.rationale: This is the exact unchecked boundary check described in the root cause. Using lcn + len directly can overflow and wrap, allowing an out-of-volume run to evade the nbits limit check.

vuln_statements.explanation: This is the unchecked volume-range validation in run_unpack(). The expression lcn + len can overflow on 64-bit arithmetic, wrap around, and incorrectly pass the boundary check against sbi->used.bitmap.nbits, allowing out-of-volume run mappings.

bic_trace_step.reason: Yes, the relevant logic is present in this function body and the overflow-prone boundary check is visible. In run_unpack(), after computing the run length and LCN, it does `if (lcn != SPARSE_LCN64 && lcn + len > sbi->used.bitmap.nbits) { /* lcn range is out of volume */ return -EINVAL; }`. This is exactly the unchecked `lcn + len` arithmetic described in the root cause. There is no overflow-safe pre-check such as `lcn > nbits - len`, nor any explicit wraparound detection before the addition. The function also lacks any fix-specific handling for 64-bit overflow in the volume-range validation, so the vulnerable construct is present and unfixed in this commit.
